passages.excerpt_preview: Over time, dilution of Tata Sons holdings left the center with small stakes in several affiliates, complicating strategic control.
Tata joined the group in 1925 without completing a university degree and later governed a highly decentralized federation of companies.
India’s licensing and monopoly-regulation regime also shaped group decisions.
Under his leadership, professional managers had considerable autonomy.
The case helps balance personal-leadership narratives with governance structure and public policy constraints.
